clue.text: A libertine enjoys embrace of favourite bird

indicators.note: the favourite holds the libertine in its arms, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a favourite, especially a teacher's favourite, is a pet
a libertine is a rake, a dissolute man

explanation.surface: A womaniser is hugged by his favourite companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enjoys embrace of' puts A RAKE inside PET.
explanation.definitionFit: A parakeet is a small long-tailed parrot, a kind of bird.

clue.text: Appeals to worker to be nice

parts.note: pleas are appeals or requests
the ant is the crossword's usual worker insect

explanation.surface: Requests to an employee to be kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Something agreeable or enjoyable is nice.

clue.text: Salesman gets chap in to deliver carpet

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: in means the chap goes inside the other piece

parts.note: to deliver from something is to rid of it
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A salesman brings a man along to deliver a rug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpet' is a verb here: to carpet someone is to give them a dressing-down.
explanation.definitionFit: To call someone onto the carpet is to scold them formally.

clue.text: Conveyance for Arthurian knight, a leader of knights

parts.note: Sir Kay was one of King Arthur's knights, his foster brother

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A knight of the Round Table needs transport fit for a leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe-like boat is a vehicle for carrying a person over water.

clue.text: Problems are mounting for Dutch scholar

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means the words climb, so problems are reads upwards

parts.note: sums are arithmetic problems

explanation.surface: Difficulties pile up for an academic from Holland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' reverses SUMS ARE in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Renaissance humanist of Rotterdam was a renowned Dutch scholar.

clue.text: Mushroom paste

explanation.surface: A fungus mashed into a pâté.
explanation.definitionFit: To mushroom is to grow and extend rapidly; a paste such as a sandwich filling is also something you smear on bread.

clue.text: Remarkable people put up plant on instalment system

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means the pieces are read from the bottom

parts.note: the anemone is a flowering plant
HP is hire purchase, buying in instalments

explanation.surface: Extraordinary folk sow flowers paid for on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses ANEMONE set on HP (a down clue) as one run. HP, hire purchase, is the British name for buying goods on instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: Extraordinary individuals are called prodigies or marvels, plural of phenomenon.

clue.text: He's into bondage!

parts.note: the surface suggests a kinky man, but the bonds are Premium Bonds and he is the machine choosing their winners

explanation.surface: A man with unusual tastes.
explanation.walkthrough: Premium Bonds are a British government savings scheme whose prize numbers are drawn by a random-number machine with a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Electronic Random Number Indicator Equipment selects Premium Bond prize winners.

clue.text: It's hard boarding grubby little boat …

indicators.note: boarding means getting on board, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: grubby means dirty or dingy
h is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Climbing into a dirty small vessel is tough.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinghy is a small open boat, often used as a tender.

clue.text: … provided by Samuel and Peter

parts.note: Peter Pan is J. M. Barrie's boy who never grows up

explanation.surface: A little boat supplied by two men, Samuel and Peter.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries over 'little boat' from the clue before as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-bottomed Chinese skiff is another small boat.

clue.text: My pet is spoilt and vain

indicators.note: spoilt suggests the letters of my pet are ruined and reshaped

explanation.surface: An owner complains that a pampered animal has become conceited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is spoilt' rearranges MYPET.
explanation.definitionFit: Vain in the sense of futile or hollow, as in empty promises or vain threats.

clue.text: Greek soldier, a heartless man, interrupts match in progress

indicators.note: breaking into the match means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a match under way is 'game on'

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter of man is dropped

parts.note: taken as the word itself before trimming

explanation.surface: A Greek warrior, a cruel fellow, bursts onto the pitch during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' trims MAN to MN, and 'interrupts' sets MN inside GAME ON, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer, the king who led the Greek army against Troy was a warrior.

clue.text: Lift your hands and catch bird quietly

parts.note: to catch, as on a nail or snag, is to stick
the emu is a large flightless Australian bird
p (piano) is the musical direction meaning quietly

explanation.surface: Instructions for snaring a bird silently with raised hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift your hands' is the robber's command; the answer is spoken words, not an action.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunman's order to raise one's arms is a hold-up command.

clue.text: Charm helps one to be ahead

indicators.note: the phrase's letters help supply the word, which sits within to be ahead

explanation.surface: A lucky charm that helps someone get ahead in life.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'to be ahead'; the surface sense of a charm bringing success is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeah is a Caribbean form of sorcery, and a charm or fetish used in it.

clue.text: Arranges to have Anne set adrift

indicators.note: adrift suggests the letters of anne set are loose and wandering into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone organises for a woman named Anne to be cast off in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adrift' rearranges ANNESET.
explanation.definitionFit: To tidy or put in order is to arrange things neatly.

clue.text: Represented in French art, see wild flower

indicators.note: represented means presented again in another form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: es is the French for 'art' as in 'thou art', tu es

explanation.surface: A wild flower depicted in a French painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Represented' rearranges ES, SEE and WILD together.
explanation.definitionFit: An Alpine plant with white woolly bracts is a familiar mountain bloom.

clue.text: Emergency with the French kind of match

parts.note: need is a time of emergency or want, as in 'in time of need'
le is the French masculine for the

explanation.surface: A crisis matched with France's definite article.
explanation.walkthrough: A needle match is a sporting contest fought with special rivalry or ill feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A grudge contest between bitter rivals is called a needle match.

clue.text: Where Cain went to sleep?

explanation.surface: Biblical query about Cain's destination after nodding off.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis says Cain went to dwell in the land of Nod; the phrase is also a jokey idiom for sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis names the region east of Eden as Cain's place of exile, and the phrase is slang for slumber.

clue.text: Family leave city, making a noise

parts.note: a clan is a family group
to go is to leave
Ur is the ancient city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A family departs town noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud continuous ringing din or racket.

clue.text: Refer to Bill briefly

explanation.surface: Mention a man called Bill in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is a printed notice; 'briefly' says the word is a shortening of advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: To advert to something is a formal way to mention it; a bill or poster is an advertisement, shortened.

clue.text: Get stuck in gear

explanation.surface: Something caught in machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get stuck in' is British for setting to work with vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle a task is to set to with energy; tackle is also equipment, as in fishing tackle.

clue.text: The stuff that waffles are made of?

definitions.text: The stuff that waffles are made of?

parts.words: The stuff that waffles are made of?
parts.note: read as cooking it asks for batter, but waffles here is evasive talk, and the stuff is a soft woollen cloth that also means such talk

explanation.surface: A question about what waffles are made of.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasive or flattering talk is called waffle, and also by the name of a soft woven cloth.

clue.text: One who started up to go down

explanation.surface: A launcher who then sinks.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who established an institution is its originator; a ship that sinks is said to founder.

clue.text: Obliged to follow a swarm

indicators.note: to follow means the obliged word comes after the other piece

parts.note: bound means obliged, as in duty-bound

explanation.surface: Being made to trail after a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To be plentiful or teem, as places that crawl with insects.

clue.text: Feel miserable down under

parts.note: to feel cold is to be cold, so feel stands for be
miserable means low in spirits

explanation.surface: Feeling depressed in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down under' looks like Australia but simply means lower down, beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Something underneath or lower down is situated beneath.

clue.text: Composer sounds like a heel

indicators.note: sounds like means the word heel's synonym is said aloud

parts.note: a ship heels or lists when it leans to one side

explanation.surface: A musician's name rhymes with a cad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heel' looks like a scoundrel but is the nautical verb, to lean over.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian Romantic pianist and composer.

clue.text: Approach to zero hour not unknown in part of Ireland

indicators.note: not means the unknown is left out

parts.note: County Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: An approaching deadline that is known in an Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: COUNTY DOWN is a county in Northern Ireland; algebra's unknowns are x, y and z.
explanation.definitionFit: A launch or deadline is preceded by counting the seconds backwards to nought.

clue.text: X — you're looking at it

explanation.surface: A reader is shown a cross mark.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle was printed in The Times newspaper, which the reader holds.
explanation.definitionFit: The multiplication sign is read as multiplied by; the newspaper carrying this puzzle is the one being read.

clue.text: International organization's committed murder, without any training

parts.note: the UN is the United Nations, with its possessive s
to commit murder is to have killed

explanation.surface: The UN is accused of murder by untrained staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker with no training lacks expertise or qualifications.

clue.text: Fruit gives a chap energy

parts.note: a chap is a man
go means energy or vigour, as in 'full of go'

explanation.surface: Eating fruit gives a man vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical stone fruit with orange flesh.

clue.text: Hate turning unruly youth out of gang

indicators.note: turning means the whole assembled piece is read backwards
the youth stands outside the gang, so the gang word sits within

parts.note: a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a rowdy 1950s British youth
a set is a group or gang of people

explanation.surface: Hatred drives a wild youth to quit his gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' puts SET inside TED, giving TSETED, and 'turning' reverses it. TEDs were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something is to feel strong hatred towards it.

clue.text: Coeur de Lion, for instance, was less polite about it

indicators.note: about means the ruder word goes around the other piece

parts.note: cruder means more vulgar, less polite
it is sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: Richard the Lionheart was rather rude about something.
explanation.walkthrough: Coeur de Lion is King Richard I of England, who fought in the Third Crusade; 'it' meaning sex appeal gives SA.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard the Lionheart went on holy war in Palestine, making him an example of such a warrior.
